subject: MAP + Acceptance Tests: success criteria, exit gates, and cutover timeline for CareVista POC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@carevista.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + key acceptance tests — request for confirmation

Alex — attaching a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (CareVista_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short checklist of acceptance tests we propose for the pilot. High level: we want to be explicit about the success criteria and the narrow set of exit gates so both teams can move to a clean go/no-go decision.

Summary (please scan):
- Pilot scope: 2 internal apps, ~10k monthly inference requests, 30 request/sec peak.
- Primary success metric: 95th percentile response latency <= 220ms for end-to-end gen flows under peak simulated load.
- Secondary metrics: embedding similarity recall >= 88% on the 100-sample validation set; token-level cost within the forecast range (+/- 15%).
- Acceptance tests (minimum):
  1) Load test at 1.5x expected peak for 2 hours without P99 spikes > 350ms.
  2) Accuracy check: 100 labeled prompts run through model variant A and B; concordance threshold >= 88%.
  3) Failover test: simulate gateway region outage — auto-fallback to warm region within 45s and no more than 5% request loss.
  4) Data handling verification: KMS-backed encryption and audit log sampling with retention demo.

Proposed exit gates (pass conditions):
- All acceptance tests marked PASS by both teams in the evidence workbook.
- Procurement & SOW accepted (basic SC/ops acceptance).
- A short cutover runbook completed and reviewed.

Tentative timeline:
- Working session to finalize criteria: week of Oct 19 (30 min)
- Load/accuracy runs: Oct 26–30
- Go/no-go decision: Nov 5

Requests: can you confirm the acceptance metrics above and whether the load profile matches your expectations? If okay, I'll schedule a 30-minute working session early next week and circulate a revised MAP with rows for owners and evidence.

Attachments: CareVista_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft)

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Rafael — thanks for the clear draft. Quick notes from my side after a fast sync with our engineering lead: 

- Latency target looks fine but can we call out whether caching is allowed for the 95th metric (we prefer measurements without artificial client-side caching).
- For the accuracy/concordance test we will supply a 100-sample labeled set; want to make sure runs are deterministic (seed & model variant documented).
- Procurement timeline attached (CareVista_procurement_timeline.xlsx) — our approvals team needs an approved SOW + any security questionnaire answered by Nov 18 to hit our fiscal deadlines.

Two asks:
1) Add a note that acceptance test runs use a defined seed and the model variant used must be recorded in the evidence workbook.
2) Can Redwood provide an instrumentation checklist for the audit log sampling? We need to ensure our compliance team signs off.

I can do the working session Oct 20 at 11am PT if that works.

-Alex Turner
Director of Product — CareVista Health

Subject: Re: MAP draft + key acceptance tests — instrumentation and pass/fail details

Alex / Rafael — I pulled together a short instrumentation checklist and updated the acceptance tests to be more concrete. Key changes below; see notes column in the attached CareVista_MAP_v1.xlsx for owners and evidence fields.

Instrumentation checklist (Redwood responsibilities unless noted):
- Trace sampling: enable distributed tracing at request entry and token-streaming boundary; sample rate 100% for acceptance runs.
- Audit logs: enable KMS-backed event logs for all inference calls; deliver 7 days of exported logs for QA review.
- Deterministic runs: we will expose a fixed RNG seed parameter and log seed in evidence workbook.
- Load harness: we will provide JMeter/Locust scenario config and the script used to run 1.5x peak.

Pass/Fail rules (examples):
- Latency test PASS if 95th <= 220ms and P99 <= 350ms across 1.5x peak run.
- Concordance PASS if recall >= 88% and no model variant shows >5% regression vs baseline.
- Failover PASS if warm-region fallback completes within 45s and error rate above baseline remains <=5%.

I also added a small runbook step for evidence handoff: we will place an indexed results CSV and the raw traces into the shared Drive folder after each run.

Action: Rafael — please confirm working session at Oct 20 11am PT (Alex proposed) and I'll add the meeting invite.

Thanks —
Monica Patel

Subject: SOW draft + proposed go/no-go date (please review)

Alex — attaching the first SOW draft (SOW-draft-CareVista.pdf). Two operational notes:

1) We propose a formal go/no-go decision meeting on Nov 30 after evidence runs complete and both teams verify the evidence workbook. That date gives CareVista time for procurement sign-off and gives Redwood a 3-week window for any regressions.
2) Payment and ramp: initial reserved capacity credit applied for pilot month; standard overage billing thereafter. Procurement has asked for a one-page summary of acceptance criteria — included in the SOW appendix for quick reference.

Links included in SOW: HubSpot deal link, draft DocuSign envelope (DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/recipient/abc123).

Next steps for us: Rafael/Monica to run the scheduled load & concordance tests Oct 26–30 and upload evidence by Nov 3 so we can review and finalize SOW items.

Ben / Rafael / Monica — all looks good from product and procurement has reviewed the timeline. A couple of small asks before we finalize: 

- Please add explicit language in the SOW appendix about data retention for logs (we require 90 days for audit logs and a sub-30-day configurable retention for temporary debug traces).
- We will provide the labeled 100-sample concordance set by Oct 22 (already in progress).
- Procurement confirms they can meet Nov 18 approval milestone if the final SOW is shared by Nov 10.

We approve the acceptance criteria as written, subject to the two small changes above. Once you update the SOW appendix and share, we'll route for signature.

Thanks for the clear process — looking forward to the pilot.
